text:
The generated opaque-script launcher now publishes its exit artifact on the same terms as AtomicFiles: umask 077 moved above every redirect so stdout/stderr are created 0600; the temporary is process-private ($$-suffixed sibling) rather than a fixed .tmp name, which matters because launch paths are deterministic in (submission key, source, invocation) and a requeued element reuses the same script; set -C prevents clobbering; contents are flushed with a portable 'sync FILE || sync || :' before the atomic rename; publication is skipped if the temporary could not be written, and the real workload status is still the script's exit code.

Evidence: extended the existing worker BatchSuite test that actually executes the generated script -- it still preserves exit 7 and reads back RemoteScriptExitRead.Exited(7), and now also asserts no surviving .tmp sibling, set -C present, a process-private temporary name, umask ordered before the first redirect, and stdout created rw-------. worker 2/2.
